intro.google.p1: Google Suggest is the list of predicted searches that appears automatically when you type a keyword into the Google search box. It reflects the phrases people actually search for and the questions and problems they have in mind, which makes it a very useful source for content creation and SEO keyword research.
intro.google.p2: With Egosaru, just enter a keyword and it collects the related Google suggestions in one go, grouped by category such as space, letters and numbers, and shows them in an easy-to-read list. No more typing "keyword + a", "keyword + b" into the search box by hand: you can map out related keywords thoroughly in a short time.
intro.google.uses: Planning the headings of a blog post or product page
Looking for long-tail keywords with search potential
Understanding the questions and problems your readers have when they search
Learning from the keyword strategy of competing sites
intro.google.p3: You can use the suggestions you collect right away for SEO work such as drafting article outlines and titles or finding ideas for FAQ content. It is free to use as often as you like, so enter a keyword and give it a try. If you sign up, you also get more advanced analysis features, such as tracking how your keywords change over time and filtering with positive and negative keywords.
intro.uses_lead: Here are some ways you can use it.
intro.bing.p1: Bing Suggest is the list of predicted searches that appears automatically when you type a keyword into the search box of Microsoft's search engine, Bing. Bing reaches many people through the default Windows browser and Microsoft Copilot search integration, and it often shows different phrases from Google Suggest. Adding Bing's own search trends to your keyword research helps you find long-tail keywords that Google-only research tends to miss.
intro.bing.p2: With Egosaru, just enter a keyword and it collects the related Bing suggestions in one go, grouped by category such as space, letters and numbers, and shows them in an easy-to-read list. No more typing letters into the search box one at a time: you can map out related keywords thoroughly in a short time.
intro.bing.uses: Seeing how your topic looks and what people want on search engines other than Google
Adding more variations to article headings and title ideas
Finding niche long-tail keywords your competitors have not targeted
intro.bing.p3: You can use the Bing suggestions you collect right away for SEO work such as drafting article outlines or finding ideas for FAQ content. It is free to use as often as you like, so enter a keyword and give it a try. If you sign up, you also get more advanced analysis features, such as tracking how your keywords change over time and filtering with positive and negative keywords.
intro.youtube.p1: YouTube Suggest is the list of predicted searches that appears automatically when you type a keyword into the YouTube search box. It reflects the keywords and topics viewers actually search for on one of the world's largest video platforms, which makes it a very useful source for choosing keywords for video titles, tags and descriptions.
intro.youtube.p2: With Egosaru, just enter a keyword and it collects the related YouTube suggestions in one go, grouped by category such as space, letters and numbers, and shows them in an easy-to-read list. No more typing "keyword + a", "keyword + b" into the search box by hand: you can map out related keywords thoroughly in a short time.
intro.youtube.uses: Finding keyword ideas for video titles and thumbnails
Understanding what viewers expect to find when they search
Brainstorming channel topics and series ideas
Collecting related terms to put in video descriptions and tags
intro.youtube.p3: You can use the YouTube suggestions you collect right away for video SEO work such as planning videos, drafting titles and optimizing descriptions and tags. It is free to use as often as you like, so enter a keyword and give it a try. If you sign up, you also get more advanced analysis features, such as tracking how your keywords change over time and filtering with positive and negative keywords.
intro.amazon.p1: Amazon Suggest is the list of predicted searches that appears automatically when you type a keyword into the Amazon search box. Amazon is also a major shopping search engine, and its suggestions include many specific keywords from people who are close to buying. That makes it a very useful source for product research and for keyword selection on e-commerce and affiliate sites.
intro.amazon.p2: With Egosaru, just enter a keyword and it collects the related Amazon suggestions in one go, grouped by category such as space, letters and numbers, and shows them in an easy-to-read list. Finding keywords for product titles and descriptions
Discovering high-intent keywords to target in affiliate articles

intro.duckduckgo.p1: DuckDuckGo Suggest is the list of predicted searches that appears when you type a keyword into the search box of DuckDuckGo, the privacy-focused search engine. Because DuckDuckGo does not keep your search history, it has been gaining users, especially among privacy-conscious people, and it can show suggestions that differ from those on Google or Bing.

intro.naver.p1: Naver Suggest is the list of autocomplete predictions that appears when you type a keyword into the search box of Naver, the most widely used search engine in South Korea. Most mobile searches in Korea happen on Naver, so its suggestions show phrasing and interests that often differ from Google.

landing.lead: Just enter a keyword and see {platform} suggestions (autocomplete) all at once, expanded with letters A–Z and numbers 0–9. Free, no sign-up required.
landing.step1_d: Type a product, place or service name, or any term you want to research, then press "Search for free".
landing.step2_d: You get the original suggestions plus those with one extra character added, such as "keyword + a", "+ b" or "+ 1", all in one view.

landing.api_text: We offer a free API that returns suggestions from search engines including {platform} as JSON. Once you are logged in, you can generate a key from "API" in the user menu.
landing.faq1_a: It is the list of predicted searches shown as you type into a search box. These are combinations of words that many people actually search for, so they are a good clue to what people want to find.
landing.faq2_a: The tool is free to use and you do not need an account. If you sign up, you can track how keywords change over time and filter results with positive and negative terms.
landing.faq3_a: It also collects the suggestions you get when you add one character after your keyword, such as "keyword + a" or "keyword + b". It saves you from typing dozens of searches by hand.
landing.faq4_q: Do the results include search volume?
landing.faq4_a: Suggestions themselves do not include search counts. The terms shown are ones with a certain amount of searches, but for exact monthly volumes, check a tool such as Google Keyword Planner.
landing.faq5_q: Why do I get zero results?
landing.faq5_a: Terms with few searches do not produce suggestions. The search engine may also temporarily block requests. Try a shorter keyword, or try again a little later.
